nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-01.prompt: A $6$ by $8$ rectangle has its vertices on a circle. Compute the area of the circle.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-02.prompt: If $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b}-\sqrt{c}}{a}$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are positive integers, compute $(a, b, c)$.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-03.prompt: Let $n = 1{,}000{,}000{,}000$. Compute the number of times $0$ appears as a digit in $n^n$.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-04.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C$ is a right angle, $AC = 5$, and $BC = 4$. Point $P$ is on $\overline{AB}$, and line segments are drawn from $P$ perpendicular to $\overline{AC}$ and $\overline{BC}$, meeting them at $Q$ and $R$, respectively. Compute the minimum value of $QR$.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-06.prompt: Find the number of positive integers less than $1000$ that contain at least one odd digit and at least one even digit.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-07.prompt: In rectangle $ABCD$, $AB = 4$, and $E$ is chosen on $AD$ so that $AE = 3.12$ and $ED = 6.88$. Compute the sum of the areas of triangles $ABE$ and $CDE$.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-08.prompt: The IML Board of Directors picks a committee from its $10$ members, and then one member of the committee is selected as a chairperson. Committees may consist of one or more members, and two committees are considered different if they have different chairpersons, even if all their members are the same. Compute the number of different committees that can be selected.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-09.prompt: Find the smallest positive integer that leaves a remainder of $18$ when divided by $19$ and a remainder of $19$ when divided by $20$.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-10.prompt: Let $f(n)$ be a function defined as follows: $f(n) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{n^2-2}{n^3} & \text{if } n \neq 0 \\ 0 & \text{if } n = 0\end{cases}$. Compute $$\sum_{n=-5}^{6} f(n).$$
nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-10.reviewNote: Official key gives 17/106, an arithmetic slip: f(6) = 34/216 = 17/108.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-11.prompt: Compute the least positive integer $n$ for which there exist an integer $m$ such that $50^5 \times n^2 = m^3$.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-12.prompt: In square $ABCD$, $E$ is on $\overline{BC}$ and $F$ is on $\overline{CD}$ so that $\overline{AE} \perp \overline{EF}$. If $AE = 4$ and $EF = 3$, compute the area of $ABCD$.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-13.prompt: The perimeter of a rectangle with integer sides is $98$. Compute the maximum area.
nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-13.reviewNote: Official key prints 60, a misprint: its own solution gives 24 x 25 = 600.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-14.prompt: Trapezoid $ABCD$ with bases $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{CD}$ is inscribed in a circle. $AB = 6$, $CD = 9$ and $BD = 11$. Find $AD$.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-15.prompt: In triangle $ABC$, $m\angle A = 60$, $m\angle B = 75$, and $BC = 6$. Compute $AB$.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-16.prompt: Set $A = \{3, 5, 8, 13, 21\}$, and set $B = \{4, 6, 9, 14, 22\}$. Compute the sum of the $25$ possible products $xy$, where $x$ is an element of $A$ and $y$ is an element of $B$.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-17.prompt: Compute the number of divisors of $6^6$ that are not divisible by $6$.

nyciml-2012-13-fall-junior-18.prompt: Given that $P(x)$ is a polynomial with nonnegative integer coefficients, and that $P(1) = 4$ and $P(5) = 1276$, compute $P(10)$.
